title: Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance - CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance - Types of Authority
subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: An agency manual states that a buyer is permitted to issue purchase orders up to $10,000 without additional approval. This is an example of which type of authority?
questions.explain: Actual Express Authority is specifically and explicitly granted to the agent by the principal, often through statutes, policies, job descriptions, or direct instruction.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: Which type of authority occurs when a third party reasonably believes an agent has the authority to bind the principal, even though the principal has not actually granted such authority, often based on the principal's actions or inaction?
questions.explain: Apparent Authority arises when the principal's behavior leads a third party to reasonably believe the agent is authorized to act, regardless of whether actual authority exists.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: In public procurement, what is the crucial legal distinction regarding 'Apparent Authority' when compared to private sector purchasing?
options: Apparent authority is stronger in the public sector.
Public entities generally cannot be bound by the apparent authority of their agents.
Elected officials are the only ones who can utilize apparent authority.
Apparent authority protects public buyers from personal liability.
questions.explain: A key tenet of public contract law is that a sovereign entity (the government) generally cannot be bound by the unauthorized acts of its employees. Therefore, unlike private corporations, public entities are rarely bound by Apparent Authority.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: A department manager without purchasing authority signs a contract with a vendor. The procurement director later reviews the contract, determines it is highly beneficial, and officially approves and signs it. What legal concept has occurred?
questions.explain: Ratification occurs when a principal retroactively approves and adopts an act performed by an agent (or non-agent) who did not have the authority to act at the time the act was performed.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: The purchasing manual gives a buyer the explicit authority to 'manage the acquisition of fleet vehicles.' The buyer, needing to verify specs, travels to a nearby dealership using an agency pool car. Though traveling wasn't explicitly mentioned in the manual, it is considered which type of authority?
questions.explain: Actual Implied Authority consists of the unwritten powers that are reasonably necessary to carry out the duties that were expressly authorized.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: Which of the following documents is the most common way a principal formally grants actual express authority to an agent?
options: A formal contract signed by a vendor
A Delegation of Authority policy or Purchasing Ordinance
questions.explain: A Delegation of Authority or a municipal purchasing ordinance officially and expressly outlines exactly what level of authority a buyer or purchasing agent has to bind the public entity.
